speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; could you please list your specific past diagnoses and when your symptoms first began?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like significant cerebellar dysfunction. To help narrow this down, when exactly did these ataxia symptoms first start, and do you have any history of head trauma, stroke, or specific genetic conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to Natalizumab therapy.

The combination of subacute gait/limb ataxia and your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is highly suggestive of PML. I need to confirm the severity of your neurological decline.
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES: Axial T2-weighted MRI of the brain.
